title.narrative: Rehabilitation of short-cycle crops production to the food and nutritional security of vulnerable people affected by Hurricane Oscar

description.narrative: Shortly after 6:00 pm on October 20 Hurricane Oscar made landfall near Baracoa, Guantánamo province, with winds exceeding 130 km/h amidst an unprecedented national energy emergency. The storm maintained a very slow movement over the eastern provinces, remaining nearly 24 hours over national territory, representing an additional risk of flooding. Several locations surpassed 300 mm of rainfall, causing severe flooding, significant infrastructure damage, and blocked roads and highways. The accumulated rainfall set historical records of 650 mm in the municipality of San Antonio del Sur, where 6 of the 7 deaths were reported and where flooding reached most of the inhabitants due to the overflowing of the Ciguatos and Sabanalamar rivers.This situation caused severe flooding, unprecedented in the affected territories. Losses in agriculture, livestock, agroforestry and fishing sectors affected a fundamental livelihood for the inhabitants of the province of Guantánamo. It was reported that severe impacts on more than 4000 hectares of vegetables, 750 hectares of bananas, 1,117 tons of beans, 4,648 hectares of coffee, 3,782 hectares of cocoa, and 153 hectares of coconut. Damage to the roofing of facilities linked to small livestock and to the infrastructure of fishery product processing centers were also identified. This adds to an already very complex situation due to the total or partial absence of electricity since last Friday, impacting water supply, potential loss of stored food, and highly limited telecommunications services. The floods could exacerbate an already complex epidemiological situation with a potential increase in arboviral diseases such as dengue or oropouche.According to the magnitude of the damage and losses caused by Hurricane Oscar with negatively impacted on food and nutritional security, not only in the short term, but also in the medium and long term, the project will focus on the rapid rehabilitation of short-cycle crop production in the most affected municipalities of the province of Guantánamo (San Antonio del Sur, Imías, Maisí y Baracoa).The availability of food is one of the main problems in this area. For this reason, it has been prioritized by the FAO in support to the government. Vegetables become even more important in times of scarcity than other foods left unsatisfied by extensive hurricane damage. That is why the government authorities have prioritized the production of vegetables among other needs to be supported immediately with CERF resources. Main support will be provided for the early rehabilitation of vegetable production of Spanish's chard, Chinese's chard, lettuce, red radish, pepper and tomato. FAO will provide technical assistance to introduce more resilient production practices focused on supporting the immediate resumption of agricultural production that the affected population needs for daily consumption, as part of their regular diet and as a good source of nutrients. This project will contribute to support 6,850 farmers by providing seeds of vegetables and some inputs to increase the production of short-cycle crops by 3,000 ha. FAO activities are aimed at curbing the deteriorating food security situation in the affected communities supporting the sources of local fresh food for the beneficiary population (140,000 beneficiaries).
